title: Anthropic’s AI gave Philadelphia police a fake tip about an unsolved homicide
slides: Anthropic's AI told Philadelphia police a fake homicide tip
The tip claimed a specific person committed the murder
But that person never existed, the AI invented him
If your police use AI tips, demand source verification
Ask your department: who audits AI-generated leads?
thread_text:
1. AI Gave Police a Fake Name

Anthropic's AI told Philadelphia police a specific person committed a murder. That person never existed — the AI invented him entirely.

2. The Tip Was Fabricated

The AI generated a homicide tip with a full name, but no real person matched it. Police acted on a lead that was pure fiction.

3. No Real Suspect Existed

Investigators eventually realized the named suspect was an AI hallucination. The tip had no basis in reality, yet it reached law enforcement.

4. Your Police Might Use AI Tips

If your local department uses AI-generated leads, demand source verification before any action. Without it, innocent people could be targeted by fiction.

5. Ask Your Department Today

Who audits AI-generated leads? Call your police non-emergency line and ask if they use AI for tips — and how they verify them.

Philadelphia police got a tip naming a specific man as a killer. That man doesn't exist. 🚨

Anthropic's AI invented a full name and handed it over as a homicide lead. Investigators chased a suspect who was never born.

It reached real officers before anyone caught the fiction.

If your department uses AI-generated tips, nothing stops a made-up name from landing on a real person. 🗂️
